# Voice cloning

- Route: `/tools/voice-cloning`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `voice-cloning`

## Summary

Record or upload 5 to 60 seconds of your own speech, create a voice, and have it read any text in more than twenty languages. (AI tools)

## Details

Voice cloning makes a reusable voice from a short recording of your own speech. Read a few natural sentences into your microphone, or upload a clip of 5 to 60 seconds, confirm that the voice is yours (or that you have the explicit permission of the person speaking), and create the voice. It appears under My voices with a short preview. From then on you can type any text, pick one of more than twenty languages and an emotion level, and get an MP3 and a WAV of that voice reading it. The model runs on a GPU server we operate, every generated file carries an inaudible watermark, and nothing you record is used to train anything.
### What it does
- Creates a saved voice from 5 to 60 seconds of speech recorded in the browser or uploaded as an audio file.
- Checks that the recording is long enough and actually contains speech before anything is counted.
- Speaks any text with the saved voice in over 20 languages, with an emotion control from calm to expressive.
- Returns the speech as an MP3, with a WAV download made in your browser.
- Marks every generated file with an inaudible watermark so synthetic speech can be identified.
### How to use it
1. Record or upload: 5 to 60 seconds of clear speech in a quiet room.
2. Confirm consent: Tick that the voice is yours, or that you have the speaker's permission.
3. Create the voice: A short preview renders and the voice is saved to your account.
4. Generate speech: Type text, pick a language and emotion, and download the audio.
### Supported formats
- Input: webm, m4a, mp3, wav, ogg, flac, mp4
- Output: mp3, wav
- The reference must be 5 to 60 seconds long and contain speech.
- Saving a voice needs an account; preset voices work without one.
### Technical details
- The voice engine is Chatterbox Multilingual (MIT licence), run on our own GPU server. It clones from the reference clip at the moment you generate; no model is trained on your voice.
- Creating a voice counts as one AI job (the preview). Each generation counts as one AI job. A request that fails or is refused is not counted.
- The length of text per request depends on your plan, at roughly 18 characters per second of speech; the counter under the text box shows your limit.
- Every generated file carries Resemble AI's PerTh watermark, which is inaudible and survives common editing and compression.
- The first request after a quiet period can take up to 20 seconds while the engine loads.
### Use cases
- Video narration: Re-read a changed line of a script without re-recording it.
- Courses and tutorials: Voice the same lesson in several languages.
- Accessibility: Have long text read aloud in a familiar voice.
- Prototyping: Hear a script read before recording the final take.
### FAQ
Q: Can I clone someone else's voice?
A: Only with that person's explicit permission. You must confirm that the voice is yours or that you have permission before a voice is created, and we store that confirmation with the voice. Impersonating someone without permission, fraud and political deepfakes are forbidden by our Terms.
Q: Will it sound exactly like me?
A: It usually sounds recognisably like the speaker, but it is not a perfect copy: accents, unusual voices and noisy recordings are harder. Record a few natural sentences in a quiet room for the best result.
Q: Is my recording used to train an AI model?
A: No. Nothing you upload or generate is used to train any model. The voice is cloned from your reference clip each time you generate speech.
Q: Can people tell the audio is generated?
A: Every file generated with a saved voice carries an inaudible watermark that detection tools can read. It does not change how the audio sounds.
Q: How do I delete a voice?
A: Open Account, Voices and delete it. Its reference recording and preview are removed; audio you already generated stays in your history until its own retention period ends.
Q: How many voices can I keep?
A: It depends on your plan; the page shows how many you have saved and your limit.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Use when someone wants text read aloud in their own voice: they record or upload 5 to 60 seconds of their speech, save a voice, and have it speak any text in over 20 languages with an emotion control.
When to send them elsewhere: To invent a new voice from a written description use Voice designer (voice-designer). To change the sound of an existing recording use Voice changer (voice-changer). To make a voice higher or lower without AI use Change Audio Pitch (change-audio-pitch).
Related tools: voice-designer (create a voice from a description); voice-changer (convert an existing recording); clean-voice-audio (clean the sample before cloning); change-audio-pitch (simple pitch shift)
